# Test fixtures

Copies, byte for byte, of measurement records that live outside this repository.
They are committed here so the tests depend on a **fixed** artefact rather than on
a mutable working path, and so a run on another machine measures the same thing.

Nothing here is regenerated by a build. If a source file changes, copy it in
again deliberately and expect the profile checksum test to change with it — that
is what the checksum is for.

| File | Copied from | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-08-26-manual-colour-brightness-points.json` | `/workspace/.hermes/measurements/2026-08-26-manual-colour-brightness-points.json`, as at 2026-08-26 | `5c9211389f8c8a661f29cadef360ab6bc223e2546b150e154aed43c581866a7e` |
| `2026-08-27-manual-colour-brightness-points-with-hue240-repeat.json` | the same mutable path, as at 2026-08-27, after the targeted hue-240 repeat was added | `a9679dfda6aebe02880f00e66d443efc619ee1a2edc0b6f5d4a10c63da7dcf62` |
| `2026-08-26-current-diffuser-before-mask-coupling.json` | `/workspace/coupling.json` (per-clock, gitignored at the repository root; JSON content preserved, line endings normalized to LF) | `b6f1e2c28869e69155c6033f9811e4878d1be62dd74781bb4e46b96ba91ed96d` |

**Both measurement records are kept.** The 2026-08-26 one pins what the model
did before the repeat existed, so a change in the numbers is visible as a
change rather than absorbed into a new baseline. The 2026-08-27 one is the
same record with eight points added; nothing in it was edited or removed.

## The measurement record

Manual visual settings supplied by Franz, taken on the clock whose optical stack
is `current-diffuser-before-mask`. Every point is a slider percentage somebody
chose by eye at a stated ambient level, for a stated hue and saturation. It is
**not** read from clock NVS: the near-light replacement ignores colour, so the
points were preserved externally.

Six drift-controlled rounds are usable, each `W-0-180-W-60-240-W-120-300-W` with
white anchors interleaved so the round can be corrected for the observer drifting
over the ten minutes it takes:

| lux | round id | white anchors | note |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 0.02 | `dark-room-0.02-lux-drift-controlled` | 30/30/30/30 | |
| 0.07 | `dark-0.07-lux-drift-controlled` | 35/35/38/35 | |
| 0.15 | *(no `roundId`; recovered by exact `logLux`)* | 40/45 | anchors at the ends only |
| 0.5 | `mid-0.5-lux-drift-controlled` | 40/40/40/40 | |
| 1.9 | `mid-1.9-lux-drift-controlled` | 50/50/50/50 | |
| 10 | `bright-10-lux-drift-controlled-ceiling-limited` | 90/90/90/90 | four hues at the 100 % ceiling |

The eight points around 2.0–2.4 lx are **not** a round: they were taken without
interleaved white anchors, at eight different ambient levels, and one of them is
at `sat=80` on a hue that is not a knot. They are superseded by the
drift-controlled 1.9 lx round and the profile records them as excluded.

## The targeted hue-240 repeat (2026-08-27 record only)

Eight further points declared as a family, `hue240-targeted-repeat-2026-08-27`,
`kind: "targeted-repeat"`, hue 240, levels 0.02/0.15/0.5/1.9. Each level is a
two-point sitting `W-H240` under its own round id `<family>-<level>`.

They are **pairs, not rounds**: two observations say nothing about the four
hues they did not look at, and the parser refuses to treat them as a round or
to fill the missing hues in. What a pair does measure well is the same-sitting
difference between its white and its colour, which is the residual with the
observer's adaptation divided out.

| lux | round | repeat | residual difference |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 0.02 | W 30/30/30/30, H240 50 % | W 25, H240 40 % | −0.0139 dec |
| 0.15 | W 40/45, H240 80 % | W 30, H240 55 % | **+0.1409 dec** |
| 0.5 | W 40×4, H240 70 % | W 40, H240 65 % | −0.0827 dec |
| 1.9 | W 50×4, H240 70 % | W 50, H240 70 % | 0.0000 dec |

Their **white anchors do not enter the global white baseline**, only their own
pair. At 0.15 lx the repeat's single anchor sits 0.56 decades below the round's,
and pooling it would drag the baseline every hue is measured against by 0.19
decades on the strength of one anchor from a session aimed at one colour. What
pooling would have done is reported in the profile under
`targeted.whiteBaseline.ifPooled` rather than left as an assertion.

## The coupling record

`scripts/lab.py calibrate` output for the same clock: the per-cell coupling map
and, the only part used here, the measured LED drive-response table. The drive
response is neither linear nor a gamma, and 20 % brightness comes out as a drive
of about seven — the part of the curve where assuming proportionality is worst.
